What if regional power pools became the engine of an equitable energy future? 
 
As development aid declines (projected to fall by up to 22% this year) the Global South is stepping up, not stepping back. 
  
South–South trade now exceeds 28% of global trade. Regional blocs are leading, not following. And across Africa, Asia, and Latin America, countries are forging energy transitions on their own terms; through regional cooperation and shared infrastructure. 
 
🌊 Laos exports 100MW of hydropower to Singapore via Thailand and Malaysia - anchoring Southeast Asia’s growing cross-border electricity market. 
 
⚡ Ethiopia supplies up to 2,000 MW of surplus power to Kenya through a high-voltage line - contributing to Kenya’s leap from 37% to 79% electrification in just 10 years. 
 
🔋 The DRC and Zambia’s Special Economic Zone will produce battery precursors at one-third the cost of similar plants in the U.S.—laying the foundation for clean-tech manufacturing in Africa. 
 
These aren’t isolated successes: they’re signals of a seismic shift. South-South cooperation isn’t just working, it’s shaping the future of global energy..

Regional integration is emerging as one of the most effective levers for expanding access, lowering costs, and building resilient, renewable energy systems at scale. To meet SDG7 by 2030, we must center these models; grounded in proximity, value and South-South leadership.
